newsitem.title: USA: Navistar to take Q4 $35 million charge.
newsitem.headline: Navistar to take Q4 $35 million charge.

text.p: Navistar International Corp said Friday it discontinued funding of its next generation truck (NGT) program, a move likely to result in a fourth quarter charge of about $35 million.

The company said it acted after being informed by the United Auto Workers that the union would not continue negotiations. Company representatives and the UAW had been in talks on a proposal to resolve key issues necessary for the NGT program to achieve adequate financial returns.

"Without resolution of certain critical issues with the UAW, the NGT product cannot be manufactured in a way that is cost competitive and provides a fair return for our shareowners," said Navistar president John Horne in a statement.
"While we are disappointed to have to discontinue the program, we will immediately pursue alternative strategies for new product development," he added.

Horne added, "We remain committed to all elements of our truck strategy, including new product development, reducing product complexity, focusing our plants to make them more efficient and achieving competitive wages, benefit and productivity levels."
Navistar's board on August 27 gave management authority to continue funding NGT providing management was convinced that talks with the UAW were moving toward a successful resolution.
